Photo 1 shows a pitched metal roof. Photo 2 frame has no roof and its top slab is still being formed.
Photo 1 has rendered and painted upper walls, but the ground floor is unrendered and patched. Photo 3 shows bare block with rough joints.
Photo 1 shows windows glazed and framed on upper floors, with a ground-floor opening apparently in place. Not visible in photos 2 and 3.

elements.observed: The three photos show different settings and construction states. Nothing confirms they are one project.

discrepancies: Photos 1 and 2 show very different construction states, so they probably are not the same building.
Photo 2 shows an open concrete frame with formwork and no roof, which contradicts 'structure and roof complete'.
Photo 3 shows unrendered block walls with messy mortar and no visible openings, which is inconsistent with a nearly finished building.
Photo 1 is ahead of the claim, with painted facades, but the ground floor is unfinished and no address or marker links it to this project.
No brochure render or plan was supplied, so the storey count and layout cannot be checked.
retake: Wide corner shot from the street showing the whole building, with a visible plot number, signboard or landmark.
Photo of the roof edge and top floor from a neighbouring vantage point, to confirm the roof exists and the storey count.
Interior photo of each floor looking along the walls, showing window openings, frames and glazing.
Same-frame shot of photo 3's wall that also shows the building corner and ground level, to place it in the project.
progress.summary: The photos do not clearly show one building. One shows a nearly finished, painted three-storey house, while another shows an unroofed concrete frame. Hold instalment 3 until the agent confirms the site with identifiable, matching photos.
